context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations at 3,000 TPS to protect merchant revenue while supporting case reviews and compliance. It ensures sub-50ms P99 latency, PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a €25k monthly budget managed by three engineers.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Core Processing System
- Fraud Analyst, Risk Manager, and Compliance & Audit Officer
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB) and ECS Fargate
- Dynamic Rule & Model Registry
- External Cardholder Data Environment (CDE) / Tokenization Vault
- AWS S3 Object Lock (WORM storage)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway to ALB: Sends authorization requests via gRPC/REST over TLS 1.3 with mTLS and OAuth2/JWT validation.
- ALB to ECS Fargate: Forwards traffic with persistent connection pooling while enforcing rate-limiting.
- Scoring Engine to External CDE: Resolves tokens via secure APIs, ensuring raw PANs never enter application memory.
- Scoring Engine to Rule & Model Registry: Cryptographically validates and hot-loads signed rules via AWS KMS.
- System to AWS S3 Object Lock: Writes decision inputs, model versions, and explanations to append-only storage.
- Users to System: Interact via secure HTTPS Web UI and internal reporting tooling.

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Container execution managed to avoid Kubernetes overhead and stay within budget.
- AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB): Handles high-throughput ingress at 3,000 TPS while maintaining low P99 tail latency.
- AWS S3 Object Lock & KMS: Provides WORM-compliant tamper-evident storage for 7-year auditability and cryptographic signature verification.
- AWS X-Ray: Implements distributed tracing to isolate bottlenecks and enforce the 50ms latency SLA.

## Rationale
This architecture leverages serverless-adjacent managed containers and externalized PCI boundaries to minimize operational burden for a three-engineer team. It guarantees high availability and strict SLAs within financial constraints while strictly isolating sensitive cardholder data.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System screens card-not-present payment authorizations at 3,000 TPS to protect merchant revenue while supporting case reviews and compliance, ensuring sub-50ms P99 latency. It is operated by a 3-engineer team within a €25,000 monthly AWS budget while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Core Processing System [externalSystem, context]
- External Cardholder Data Environment (CDE) / Tokenization Vault [externalSystem, context]
- AWS S3 Object Lock [externalSystem, context]
- Dynamic Rule & Model Registry [externalSystem, context]
- Fraud Analyst, Risk Manager, Compliance & Audit Officer [person, context]
- Scoring Engine Container [container, Rust/Tokio, AWS ECS Fargate]
- Case Management Container [container, Node.js/TypeScript, AWS ECS Fargate]
- Fallback Scoring Container [container, Python/FastAPI, AWS ECS Fargate]
- Audit Reporting Container [container, Node.js/TypeScript, AWS ECS Fargate]

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Core Processing System -> Scoring Engine Container (gRPC/REST over TLS 1.3 with mTLS and OAuth2/JWT)
- Scoring Engine Container -> External Cardholder Data Environment (CDE) / Tokenization Vault (Secure APIs)
- Scoring Engine Container -> Dynamic Rule & Model Registry (AWS KMS and ECDSA P-256)
- Scoring Engine Container -> AWS S3 Object Lock (AWS Firehose / S3 API)
- Scoring Engine Container -> Fallback Scoring Container (Internal HTTP/JSON via AWS Service Discovery)
- Fraud Analyst / Risk Manager -> Case Management Container (HTTPS Web UI)
- Compliance & Audit Officer -> Audit Reporting Container (HTTPS Web UI)
- Audit Reporting Container -> AWS S3 Object Lock (AWS SDK / S3 API)

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Chosen for container compute to ensure predictable sub-50ms P99 latency and secure mTLS termination without Lambda cold-start overhead.
- Rust / Tokio: Chosen for the Scoring Engine to handle high-throughput (3,000 TPS) memory-efficient real-time processing.
- Node.js / TypeScript: Chosen for Case Management and Audit Reporting containers to accelerate UI-driven feature delivery.
- Python / FastAPI: Chosen for the Fallback Scoring Container for rapid execution of simplified heuristic rules during primary outages.
- AWS S3 Object Lock: Chosen for WORM-compliant storage guaranteeing 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

## Rationale
The containerized architecture separates the ultra-low-latency Rust scoring core from administrative workflows, satisfying strict performance and security isolation boundaries. Leveraging managed AWS services on ECS Fargate maintains high availability and PCI-DSS compliance within the 3-engineer operational capacity and fixed budget constraints.

Scoring Engine Container.analysis:
## Overview
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System screens card-not-present payment authorizations at 3,000 TPS to protect merchant revenue while supporting case reviews and compliance, ensuring sub-50ms P99 latency.
- Built on AWS ECS Fargate in eu-west-1, the architecture processes transactions securely while strictly adhering to PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Core Processing System
- External Cardholder Data Environment (CDE) / Tokenization Vault
- AWS S3 Object Lock
- Dynamic Rule & Model Registry
- Scoring Engine Container (Rust / Tokio, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Container (Node.js / TypeScript, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Fallback Scoring Container (Python / FastAPI, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Audit Reporting Container (Node.js / TypeScript, AWS ECS Fargate)
- API Ingress Component (Rust / Tonic gRPC)
- Token Resolution Component (Rust / Reqwest)
- Rule & Model Execution Component (Rust / Native Eval)
- Audit Dispatcher Component (Rust / Tokio async channel)
- Circuit Breaker & Fallback Coordinator Component (Rust / custom Tokio-native wrapper)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Core Processing System -> Scoring Engine Container: Sends payment authorization requests [gRPC/REST over TLS 1.3 with mTLS and OAuth2/JWT]
- Scoring Engine Container -> External Cardholder Data Environment (CDE) / Tokenization Vault: Resolves tokens securely [Secure APIs]
- Scoring Engine Container -> Dynamic Rule & Model Registry: Cryptographically validates and hot-loads signed rules [AWS KMS and ECDSA P-256]
- Scoring Engine Container -> AWS S3 Object Lock: Writes decision inputs, model versions, and explanations [AWS Firehose / S3 API]
- Scoring Engine Container -> Fallback Scoring Container: Routes to fallback during primary outages [Internal HTTP/JSON via AWS Service Discovery]

## Technology Stack
- Rust / Tokio: Selected for Scoring Engine Container to deliver sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS with memory safety.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Provides container orchestration with predictable scaling and fixed infrastructure budgeting.
- AWS KMS & ECDSA P-256: Ensures cryptographic validation for zero-downtime hot-loaded fraud rules.
- AWS S3 Object Lock: Guarantees tamper-evident, WORM-compliant 7-year audit retention.
- Node.js / TypeScript: Powers Case Management and Audit Reporting containers for rapid administrative development.

## Rationale
- The Rust-based Scoring Engine combined with non-blocking async channels guarantees performance, latency, and memory safety under high transaction loads.
- AWS-managed services and strict compliance controls securely satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1, 7-year auditability, and budgetary limits.

Case Management Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management Container supports fraud analyst reviews, administrative workflows, and risk monitoring for card-not-present payment authorizations. It securely handles suspicious payment cases while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and UI data masking.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (Person)
- Risk Manager (Person)
- Case UI Component (React / TypeScript SPA via AWS S3/CloudFront)
- Case API Component (Node.js / Express on AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Ingestion Worker Component (Node.js / TypeScript on AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Database Component (AWS Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL)
- AWS SQS (Managed Message Queue)

## Relationships
- Fraud Analyst -> Case UI Component (HTTPS Web UI)
- Risk Manager -> Case UI Component (HTTPS Web UI)
- Fraud Analyst -> Case API Component (HTTPS / REST over TLS 1.3)
- Risk Manager -> Case API Component (HTTPS / REST over TLS 1.3)
- Case API Component -> Case Database Component (PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS 1.3)
- Scoring Engine Container -> Case Ingestion Worker Component (AWS SQS over TLS 1.3 with AWS KMS)
- Case Ingestion Worker Component -> Case Database Component (PostgreSQL Wire Protocol over TLS 1.3)

## Technology Stack
- Node.js / TypeScript: Powers lightweight backend services and ingestion workers on AWS ECS Fargate.
- React / TypeScript: Delivers responsive single-page application dashboards served via AWS S3 and CloudFront.
- AWS Aurora Serverless v2 PostgreSQL: Provides cost-effective, auto-scaling relational storage for case reviews and audit logs.
- AWS SQS: Enables decoupled, asynchronous ingestion of suspicious transactions with Dead-Letter Queue support.
- AWS KMS: Secures data encryption at rest across storage and queuing layers.

## Rationale
This architecture fits the requirements by maintaining strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance through data masking and tokenized references without handling raw PANs. Additionally, managed serverless components keep operations maintainable for a three-engineer team within the €25,000 monthly budget.

## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations at 3,000 TPS to detect fraud while enabling analyst case reviews and compliance auditing. It ensures sub-50ms P99 latency and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance within a 25,000 EUR monthly AWS budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst (Person)
- Risk Manager (Person)
- Compliance & Audit Officer (Person)
- Payment Gateway / Core Processing System (External System)
- External Cardholder Data Environment (CDE) / Tokenization Vault (External System)

- Dynamic Rule & Model Registry (External System)
- Scoring Engine Container (Rust / Tokio, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Container (Node.js / TypeScript, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Fallback Scoring Container (Python / FastAPI, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Audit Reporting Container (Node.js / TypeScript, AWS ECS Fargate)

- Scoring Engine Container -> Dynamic Rule & Model Registry (AWS KMS and ECDSA P-256)
- Scoring Engine Container -> AWS S3 Object Lock (AWS Firehose / S3 API)
- Scoring Engine Container -> Fallback Scoring Container (HTTPS over mTLS via AWS Service Discovery/App Mesh)

- Risk Manager -> Case Management Container (HTTPS Web UI)
- Compliance & Audit Officer -> Audit Reporting Container (HTTPS Web UI)
- Audit Reporting Container -> AWS S3 Object Lock (AWS SDK / S3 API)

## Technology Stack

- Rust / Tokio: High-performance low-latency runtime for the Scoring Engine
- Node.js / TypeScript: Rapid administrative and auditing interface development
- Python / FastAPI: Lightweight heuristic evaluation during primary outages
- AWS S3 Object Lock: WORM storage ensuring 7-year tamper-evident auditability

## Rationale
This architecture uses high-performance Rust for real-time scoring to meet the stringent sub-50ms P99 latency constraint at 3,000 TPS. ECS Fargate and multi-tier containerization ensure strict PCI-DSS Level 1 security, fault-tolerant fallback handling, and robust 7-year auditability within fixed infrastructure budgets.

Audit Reporting Container.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System screens card-not-present payment authorizations at 3,000 TPS to protect merchant revenue while supporting case reviews and compliance, ensuring sub-50ms P99 latency. It provides a dedicated audit reporting architecture that securely indexes and queries 7-year WORM-compliant transaction logs for compliance officers and risk managers.

## Key Elements
* Compliance & Audit Officer [person]
* Risk Manager [person]
* Audit Reporting Container [container] (Node.js / TypeScript, AWS ECS Fargate)
* Audit UI Component [component] (Express.js / React SSR)
* Query & Aggregation Component [component] (TypeScript)
* S3 Access Component [component] (AWS SDK for JavaScript)
* Regulatory Exception Component [component] (TypeScript)
* AWS S3 Object Lock [externalSystem]

## Relationships
* Compliance & Audit Officer -> Audit UI Component: Interacts for secure dashboards and export packages [HTTPS]
* Risk Manager -> Audit UI Component: Monitors portfolio risk metrics and aggregated reports [HTTPS]
* Compliance & Audit Officer -> Regulatory Exception Component: Attaches compliance sign-offs and overrides [HTTPS]
* Query & Aggregation Component -> AWS S3 Object Lock: Queries historical decisions and Parquet-compacted data via Athena [AWS SDK / Athena / S3 API]
* Regulatory Exception Component -> AWS S3 Object Lock: Writes immutable exception sidecar objects [AWS SDK / S3 API]
* S3 Access Component -> AWS S3 Object Lock: Retrieves WORM-compliant logs securely [AWS SDK / S3 API]

## Technology Stack
* Node.js / TypeScript: Powers the Audit Reporting Container runtime for rapid UI and API development
* AWS ECS Fargate: Runs serverless containers within a strict €25,000 monthly infrastructure budget
* AWS S3 Object Lock & Glacier: Provides tamper-evident WORM storage for 7-year auditability with automated lifecycle transitions
* AWS Athena & Apache Parquet: Enables cost-effective, high-performance querying over partitioned historical audit data
* AWS KMS: Secures encryption-at-rest (`SSE-KMS`) for sensitive audit data, queries, and sidecar metadata

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless AWS services and columnar storage (Parquet/Athena) to meet strict 7-year auditability and PCI-DSS compliance requirements while staying within budget. Component decomposition and role-based access control isolate sensitive compliance sign-offs and ensure secure, low-latency reporting for auditors.
